sentences.text: The plaintiff has filed the suit against the defendants No.1 and 2 for recovery of Rs.7,80,000/- with interest at 18% p.a. from the date of suit till its realization with costs.

2. The suit of the plaintiff is that:
The plaintiff was the lawful tenant under the defendant No.1 in respect of residential premises No.8, 3rd Floor, 7th Main, Brindavana Nilaya, Kamadenu Layout, B.
Narayana Pura, Bengaluru for 9 years by virtue of rental agreement dated 10.04.2011 initially at a monthly rent of Rs.5,500/- and he has paid a sum of Rs.40,000/-
towards security deposit and later, rent was enhanced to Rs.11,000/- p.m.
The defendant No.1 was also residing in the same building in first floor.

During the year 2017, the defendant No.1 has introduced his friend the defendant No.2 to the plaintiff at Murageshpalya and in view of financial difficulties of defendant No.2, the defendant No.1 told the plaintiff to lend loan as the defendant No.1 would be guarantor and hence, the plaintiff agreed and paid him a sum of Rs.4 lakh when it was convinced that the defendant No.2 managing a lodge in the name of 'Palke Lodge' and further he is also going to purchase a building for Rs.60 lakh to 70 lakh to start a Paying Guest room and also doing various business and also said that the amount would be refunded within 15 days.

At that time, the defendant No.1 said that he had already given Rs.5 to 6 lakh to the defendant No.2.
3.

In the plaint, it is further stated that as the request of the plaintiff seeking return of his loan amount not heeded by the defendants, when the defendants instead demanded additional loan amount, the plaintiff came to know that both the defendants No.1 and 2 colluded and played fraud and avoided to repay the loan amount to the plaintiff.

4. In the plaint, it is further stated that as against loan of Rs.4 lakh, the defendant No.2 gave him a cheque for Rs.5 lakh bearing No.933044 dated 24.10.2017 drawn on Corporation Bank, Air Port Branch, Murgeshpalya Air Port Road, Bengaluru and on its presentation to the banker/ State Bank,
Bengaluru, it was dishonoured vide endorsement dated 01.11.2017 as 'fund insufficient' and at that time, the defendant No.1 prevented the plaintiff from filing cheque bounce case by assuring him that he would give back the money.

5. In the plaint, it is further stated that subsequent requests made by the plaintiff went in deaf ears of the defendant No.1, and the defendant No.1 in turn, forced the plaintiff to vacate the premises by making hectic efforts to dispossess the plaintiff by way of disconnecting the water supply and electricity and also by putting him in fear of criminally intimidating him with life and property.

sentences.text: 6. In the plaint, it is further averred that the defendant No.1 gone to the extent of calling his in-laws in order to make false and frivolous allegations about the plaintiff and also poked his nose into the family affairs of the plaintiff and his wife, thereby the relationship of plaintiff and his wife strained and moreover, the defendant No.1 as on 10.08.2018, disconnected the power supply and water supply in order to further harass the plaintiff and further, not allowed the plaintiff to park his vehicles at the regular parking area of the house and further used to send goondas to his office to create nuisance, so that the plaintiff should lose his job.

The defendant No.1 has sent legal notice during the month of September 2018 to the plaintiff to vacate the premises by making false allegations, for which the plaintiff gave suitable reply that the defendant No.1 shall repay the money of Rs.4 lakh, for which the defendant No.1 has not sent any reply.

7. In the plaint, it is further averred that in respect of inhuman and high handedness of the defendant no.1, the plaintiff finding no alternative, approached the jurisdictional Police and lodged a complaint and the Police have registered NCR No.782/2018 and the Police called both the plaintiff and defendant No.1 and warned the defendant No.1 not to repeat the same, but the defendant No.1 has not stopped his high handed acts and hence, the plaintiff has filed a private complaint in PCR No.55576/2019 for the offences punishable u/s.406, 420, 506B r/w Sec.34 of IPC before the learned XXIX ACMM, Bengaluru and the matter referred for investigation u/s.156(3) of Cr.P.C and it is still pending.
Due to the torture given by the defendant No.1, the plaintiff had no option to vacate the said premises.
The defendants No.1 and 2 have conspired and deceived the plaintiff for the amount of Rs.4 lakh and

in view of the fact that the cheque given by the defendant No.2 was bounced and as the defendant No.1 stood as guarantor for the loan amount taken by the defendant No.2, both are jointly and severally liable to repay Rs.5 lakh including the amount actually paid by the plaintiff and the additional sum assured by the defendants along with interest, damages and costs.
The notice sent to the defendant No.1 was duly served and the notice sent to the defendant No.2 returned with endorsement 'not claimed, returned to the sender'.
The defendant No.1 gave untenable reply.

8. In the plaint, it is further stated that the cause of action for the suit arose on the date of advancement of Rs.4 lakh on 17 th, 18th and 19th of August 2017 and also on the date when the defendants failed to return the sum as assured and also on the date of dishonour of cheque issued by the defendant No.2 drawn in Corporation Bank, Air Port Road branch, Bengaluru and also on the dates of demands made by the plaintiff to repay the amount and also on the date of issuance of legal notice on 11.06.2020, the date on which legal notice received by the defendants and on their failure to repay the loan amount.

Accordingly, the plaintiff is entitled for principal loan amount of Rs.5 lakh, agreed rate of interest at 18% p.a. from the date of payment by the plaintiff till July 2020 amounting to Rs.2,62,500/- and also the legal notice and litigation charges etc. amounting to Rs.17,500/-.
Accordingly, the plaintiff prays to decree the suit for total sum of Rs.7,80,000/- with interest at 18% p.a. and costs of suit as sought for.

sentences.text: After service of summons, the defendant No.1 appeared through Sri. G.C.S, Advocate and filed written statement.
The summons to defendant No.2 through RPAD returned with the endorsement 'not claimed' and hence, service of summons to defendant No.2 is held as sufficient.

10. In the written statement, the defendant No.1 has denied the entire plaint averments regarding loan of Rs.4 lakh lent by the plaintiff in favour of defendant No.2 at the recommendation of defendant No.1 and the defendant No.2 agreed to repay the amount and gave cheque for Rs.5 lakh as against the loan of Rs.5 lakh.

It is further denied that the plaintiff had lent the loan of Rs.4 lakh to the defendant No.2 by giving cheque leaves for Rs.2 lakh each, out of them, one cheque was bounced, for which the plaintiff subsequently gave Rs.2 lakh by way of online transfer to the account of the defendant No.2.
11.
It is further denied that the defendants No.1 and 2 have conspired together and deceived the plaintiff without repaying the loan of Rs.4 lakh.

It is denied that the defendant No.1 troubled the plaintiff to vacate his rental house and also troubled by disconnecting the water supply and electricity supply to the rented house in which the plaintiff resided.
It is further denied that the plaintiff and his family were put under threat criminally by the defendant No.1.
It is further denied in the written statement that the defendant No.1 was given Rs.40,000/- as security amount for the rented house.

12. In the written statement, the defendant No.1 further stated that the plaintiff started residing as a tenant of the house without paying rent from the month of June 2018 and hence, the defendant No.1 having no alternative, caused legal notice to vacate the house premises for which, the plaintiff has sent untenable reply and thereafter the plaintiff has falsely filed PCR 5576/2019.
The defendant No.1 never stood as guarantor for the alleged loan of R.4 lakh taken by the defendant No.2 from the plaintiff.

There is no cause of action to file the suit against the defendant No.1 in respect of alleged loan amount when there was only formal relationship of plaintiff and defendant No.1 in view of the fact that the plaintiff was tenant in the house of defendant No.1.
13.

In the written statement, the defendant No.1 further stated that the plaintiff being the tenant paid rent to the defendant No.1 till May 2018 and thereafter stopped paying rent from the month of June 2018 and became a chronic defaulter.

The plaintiff has in the month of October 2018, vacated the house premises without paying arrears of rent amount and painting charges, which the plaintiff was liable to pay after adjusting Rs.40,000/- security deposit paid by him.
The plaintiff has filed the suit with malafide intention to gain wrongfully and to extract money from the defendant No.1 by suppressing false facts and also by creating false story.

Hence, the defendant No.1 prays to dismiss the suit with exemplary costs u/s.35(a) of CPC.
14.
The plaintiff got examined himself as P.W.1 and examined a witness as P.W.2 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.22.

On the other hand, the defendant No.1 got examined himself as D.W.1 and got marked Exs.D.1 to 3.
15.
The learned counsel for plaintiff has field written arguments.
Heard the arguments of counsel for defendant No.1 .

sentences.text:
On basis of pleadings of both plaintiff and defendants, the following issues have been framed:
1) Whether the plaintiff proves that the defendant No.1 requested him to pay a sum of Rs.4 lakh loan to defendant No.2?
2) Whether the plaintiff proves that the defendant No.1 assured and undertaken that in the event if the defendant No.2 fails to make payment, he would repay the same to plaintiff and he would take entire responsibility of the said amount?
3) Whether the plaintiff proves that defendants No.1 and 2 assured to repay the amount within 15 days and they would also pay interest on the said amount?

4) Whether the plaintiff proves that on assurance made by the defendant No.1, he has issued two cheques for Rs.4 lakh to the defendant No.2, upon receipt of which the defendant No.2 issued plaintiff a cheque for Rs.5 lakh?

5) Whether the plaintiff proves that the defendant No.2 assured to repay the said sum of Rs.4 lakh within a period of 15 days and get back the cheque, failing which authorized the plaintiff to present the cheque gi9ven for Rs.5 lakh for encashment?
6) Whether the plaintiff proves that the defendant No.1 fails to make the payment,
presented cheque for encashment in Corporation Bank, Airport Road branch, which came to be dishonoured with an endorsement 'funds insufficient?
7) Whether the plaintiff proves that defendants No.1 and 2 jointly and severally are liable to pay a sum of Rs.7,80,000/- to the plaintiff?
 8) What order/ decree?
17.

My answer to the above points are as follows:
 Point No.1: Partly affirmative,
 Point No.2: Negative,
 Points No.3 & 4: Partly affirmative,
 Point No.5: Affirmative,
 Points No.6 & 7: Partly affirmative,
 Point No.8: As per final order,
 for the following:
 REASONS 18.
Points No.1 to 7: These issues are discussed together to avoid repetition of facts and evidence.

58.

Therefore, mere issuance of legal notice and reply notice in between the plaintiff and the defendant No.1 does not prove that the defendant No.1 stood as a guarantor for loan of Rs.4 lakh lent by the plaintiff in favour of defendant No.2 and when the plaintiff insisted the defendant No.1 to repay the said loan amount, the defendant No.1 told the plaintiff that in order to repaying of the said loan amount, a sum of Rs.1,000/- is reduced on the monthly rent payable by the plaintiff.

59. In view of the aforesaid oral and documentary evidence and in view of the pleading of the plaintiff, I deem it fit to hold that even the evidence of P.W.2 regarding his actual presence at the time of lending loan of Rs.4 lakh by the plaintiff in favour of the defendant No.2 on absolute assurance of defendant No.1 as a guarantor is not acceptable and trustworthy.

60. Therefore, as the documentary evidence placed on record are corroborative to the oral evidence of P.W.1 with the plaint pleading with regard to the fact that the transaction of loan of Rs.4 lakh was between the plaintiff and the defendant No.2 only, it is further held that the defendant No.1 cannot be made liable to pay the said loan amount jointly and severally.

61. Merely because there is evidence regarding acquaintance of P.W.2 with the plaintiff and the defendants No.1 and 2 as the P.W.2 also for some times being the friend of plaintiff No.1 went to the building of the defendant No.1, it does not mean that the evidence of P.W.2 is trustworthy to come to the conclusion that the defendant No.1 was the guarantor for loan of Rs.4 lakh taken by the defendant No.2 from the plaintiff.

62. In view of the entire oral and documentary evidence in relation to the facts and circumstances of the suit, it is further held that there is variance in the pleadings and evidence regarding loan liability of the defendant No.1.

Hence, as the plaintiff has by way of oral and documentary evidence proved that he has lent loan of Rs.4 lakh in favour of the defendant No.2 and in turn, gave a cheque for Rs.5 lakh as security as on the date of advancing the loan on 17.08.2017, the plaintiff is entitled for recovery of Rs.4 lakh from that date with an interest of 12% p.a. till the date of realization and also legal notice and litigations charges of Rs.17,500/- from the defendant No.2 only as against the suit claim of Rs.7,80,000/-.
